newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool indicator rises 6 cents to 713c/kg.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool indicator rises 6 cents to 713c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose six cents to 713 cents a kg clean on Wednesday at sales in Sydney and Melbourne, Wool International said.
Merino fleece was mostly dearer, with 19/21 micron one percent dearer, 20m up to one percent dearer, 22m two percent dearer, 23m unchanged and 24/25/26m 0.5 percent dearer.
Merino skirtings of 19/20m were generally unchanged, with 21/22m slightly dearer.
In crossbreds, 27m was 0.5 percent cheaper, 28/29/31m unchanged, and 30m 1.5 percent dearer.
In cardings, lambs were fully firm, locks slightly cheaper and crutchings one percent cheaper.
WI said Japanese interests including China were principal buyers with good support from Western Europe and Taiwan.
Of the 29,250 bales offered, 8.8 percent were passed in.
In early Fremantle trading, merino fleece of 20m was fully firm, 21/22/23m 1.5 percent dearer and 24m one percent dearer, while merino skirtings were generally unchanged.
Sales continue on Thursday in Sydney and Fremantle with about 37,150 bales to be offered.
